newsitem.title: CROATIA: Podravka signs DM60 mln loan at Libor +2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Podravka signs DM60 mln loan at Libor +2.5 pct.

text.p: Croatia's food giant Podravka on Wednesday signed a deal for a 60 million German mark five-year loan with Bayerishe Vereinsbank at 2.5 percent over Libor.

"The loan was issued without government guarantees because the lender decided that Podravka's business and perspectives provided enough guarantee," company president Zvonimir Majdancic said at the signing ceremony.
Bayerische had already lent it 6.3 million marks with guarantees from Germany's Hermes agency for financing capital investments during 1992-93, the company said in a news release.
German bank officials described the total interest charged to Podravka, now 5.75 percent a year, as a benchmark for commercial lending to Croatian food corporations so far.
It will be granted a one-year grace period.
Podravka will use the 60 million marks to restructure some of its outstanding short-term loans, raised mostly from Croatian banks at high interest, in a bid to reduce overall costs, Majdancic said.
In this way it hopes to reduce the interest on its debts to below 10 percent this year from 22 percent at the end of 1996.
It was paying 38.11 percent on some 563 million kuna in liabilities at the beginning of last year, but has since managed to swap out most of the old loans for cheaper ones.
Last week the company said it would soon raise 20 million marks at 4.2 percent from Bank Austria for financial restructuring. That loan will be guaranteed by the Croatian goverment.
Podravka's shares closed at 245 kuna on Wednesday on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, where they are traded in the segment for semi-regulated companies.
But rumours about disappointing consolidated results for 1996 have the share price down from 305 kuna recorded in May. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
